Maintaining proper driving speed and paying attention to the traffic condition ahead may reduce pressure and risky behaviors for the motorist while improving traffic safety.
Because of poor visibility and lighting condition, weak visual range and uncertain road condition in the tunnel, vehicles shall turn on the headlight.
Two vehicles arrive at an intersection without traffic lights at the same time and head toward different directions. If both vehicles are going straight, the one on the left has the right-of-way.
Before leaving on a motorcycle, the rider should check the surrounding traffic and the road condition first, and yield to the pedestrians and vehicles on the road before accelerating.
Do not cut into other lanes recklessly or zigzag around other vehicles just for fun. It will cause interference for vehicles behind.
Do not make sudden brakes while in high speed. It may cause rearend collisions.
Continuously speeding and braking while the vehicle is in high-speed can demonstrate my driving skills.
Do not cut into another lane suddenly when the traffic is slowing down, do not cut into another lane suddenly. Traffic from behind may not stop in time and cause collisions.
When turning from an alley to the main road, the motorist should stop completely, look around, and then proceed after making sure it is safe to go.
Drivers don't need to have first-aid knowledge. All they need is good driving skills.
If an accident victim is unconscious, you should shake and pat the victim in order to help them regain consciousness.
Intentionally causing death or injuries while riding a motorcycle, the rider could be charged with manslaughter or assault.
There is a traffic accident and someone is injured. Since no one is around, it is ok to just leave the agonizing victim behind and keep going because you are in a hurry.
Most traffic accidents are caused by the motorists' negligence, mistakes and bad driving habits.
Consuming alcohol reduces a motorist's vision and reflexes, which will increase accident rates.
When approaching a crosswalk without traffic lights on a motorcycle, the rider should reduce the speed.
A motorcycle rider needs to pay attention to the traffic lights only and not the instructions from the volunteer traffic police.
As long as a motorcycle functions well and the rider is skillful, the rider can take the motorcycle on any road, including fast lanes and the freeway.
If I am carrying a passenger on the motorcycle, I need to be very careful because I am responsible for the passenger's life.

Bad driving habits are accumulated from incorrect and inappropriate road conducts, such as tailgating, cutting and changing lanes recklessly, cutting while turning, speeding, or rushing through the road.
Drivers on the road must pay attention to safety at all times.
A motorcycle shall avoid of following large vehicles too closely from behind or on the sides. It would be too difficult to respond to emergency situations.
When the brakes are making abnormal noises, it is a normal phenomenon. There is no need for repair.
When the brakes are making abnormal noises, it is not normal. The brakes should be checked and repaired.
Not causing traffic accidents and not violating traffic regulations are the main conditions for safe driving.
A motorcycle rider make U-turns anywhere as long as there is enough room.
When a motorcycle is going through a crosswalk and there are people crossing it, the motorcycle can still go through the empty space between pedestrians.
When passing through a crosswalk without traffic signals, the rider can speed through without slowing down, in order to prevent traffic jam.
It is not necessary to replace a helmet if there is no obvious damage after sustaining heavy impact.

The purpose for the brake signal on the back of the motorcycle is to let motorists behind know your intention. A broken brake signal is often neglected. Rushing off to the road with the broken light may confuse the drivers behind and cause collisions.
If the throttle on the motorcycle is too loose or too tight, it is not normal and should be repaired immediately.
Riders should check the brakes on the motorcycle before starting the trip. If the brakes are not working normally, do not make emergency brakes and repair them immediately.
Using hand held mobile devices while riding a motorcycle is dangerous. It is a distraction that may throw the driver off balance which cause accidents.
Using mobile devices or computers to send messages while riding on a motorcycle or waiting for the red light helps us save time and connect to the world.
Before braking a motorcycle, the throttle should be moved back to null and zero output position from the engine.
Yielding to pedestrians is a display of good driving ethics.
Abiding by the traffic regulations has nothing to do with driving ehics.
Yielding and tolerance are indicators of good driving ethics.
Although drivers have the right of way when they have a greenlight, they are still required to watch out for jaywalkers and vehicles that run through red lights.
Inspecting our cars to make sure they are in good condition before we drive and yielding to pedestrians and other vehicles when on the road displays good driving ethics.
If a driver overtakes me to avoid getting dusty, I should pass them for the same reason.
If a person doesn't use common courtesy when driving, it could cause a tragedy, not only for him/herself but for everybody.
When you see the elderly and children walking slowly across the pedestrian crosswalk, you should tap your horn to warn them to hurry up.

Drivers must slow down and follow the traffic signs and signals when they approach factories, schools, hospitals, railroad stations, auditoriums, recreation areas, exhibition halls, arenas, and all other public gathering areas.
If your vehicle hits a pedestrian by accident, but the pedestrian is not injured, you can speed away to avoid trouble.
When driving at night, you should use the high-beam headlight and constantly honk your horn to warn other vehicles get out of your way.
Police officers and traffic controllers, who enforce the traffic rules, are trouble makers.
If the police catch you breaking the traffic rules, you should speed away quickly to avoid being given a citation.
Even if there is no traffic cop around, drivers are still required to follow traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings.
Although in today's society time is money, we should understand speeding often causes tragedy and life is so precious.
When driving through a tunnel, you should turn on your lights, slow down, and not change lanes.
Drivers must remain calm and concentrate on the traffic conditions when they are on the road.
After drinking alcohol, vision, hearing, and judgment become slow and impaired. Nevertheless, drinking alcohol is a good way to relax, so it is okay to drive a motorcycle after drinking.
Drivers should not drive side-by-side and talk to each other because it will dangerously affect their ability to concentrate on the road and their driving.
When driving a motorcycle, you should never speed or lose your concentration on the road, not even for one second.
If your vehicle starts having mechanical problems, that may endanger the safety of yourself or others, you can continue driving anyway.
Traffic rules are designed to maintain the smooth flow of traffic and ensure safety. Therefore, all drivers must familiarize themselves with and abide by the traffic rules.
Motorcycles are not permitted to drive along with a convoy of onduty police or security vehicles.
Drivers need outstanding skills only. Following traffic rules is not really that important.
When an accident occurs, drivers are required to cooperate with the police throughout the accident investigation process.
Drivers must park their vehicle in accordance with regulations regarding hours, spaces, and any other regulations stipulated by the local government.
Traffic police who enforce traffic rules are causing inconvenience for drivers.
Drivers may not pass vehicles from the right or pass by driving in the oncoming traffic lane if there is oncoming traffic.
Drivers have to be extremely cautious at intersections, when making turns, or when there is oncoming traffic.
Traveling up or down a steep hill, drivers have to slow down and are not allowed to stop, make a U-turn, or pass other vehicles.
Though motorcycles are smaller than automobiles and are easier to maneuver in and out of traffic, motorcyclists may not drive recklessly.
The higher the motorcycle speed, the longer the braking distance.
Drivers are required to slow down prior to braking if the road is wet.
Drivers may cross the solid double yellow lines into the oncoming traffic lane in order to pass another vehicle.

If drivers encounter an accident on the road, they must report it to the police immediately and provide assistance to the victims, not just be a bystander. If they see the vehicle that caused the accident, they must report it to the police at once.
Motorcyclists may pass another vehicle when there is oncoming traffic.
If motorcycle causes an accident, the parties involved must report it to the police immediately.
Motorcyclists may race side-by-side on the road because motorcycles are small and easy to operate.
If the vehicle behind you passes you, for safety reasons, you should not then pass that vehicle.

If a driver has to brake quickly, especially by using the emergency brake, they have to take all possible measures to protect their passengers and their vehicle from being rear-ended (hit from behind).
Drivers must park on the right side of the road to either load or unload goods and may not under any circumstances obstruct traffic.
Being considerate, showing common courtesy, and having self-control are the minimum requirements for being a good motorcycle driver.
If you have regular maintenance done on your motorcycle, it's not necessary to make sure your bike is mechanically sound before driving it each time.
It is easy to fall when making emergency brakes on a motorcycle. Therefore, it is important to follow the speed limit.
You should never drive side-by-side with other vehicles to chat with other drivers and never pass another vehicle when you are turning.
To avoid causing an accident or flipping over, drivers should not pass another vehicle on a railroad crossing and not race other vehicles.
If your vehicle breaks down on a railroad crossing, you must push your vehicle off the tracks before attempting to repair it.
For safety reasons, drivers have to look for pedestrians when they are entering or leaving an alley or the driveway of a building.

If your vehicle breaks down on a bridge, in a tunnel, near a hydrant, in front of a barrier, in a circular intersection, on a railroad crossing, in an intersection, on a pedestrian crosswalk, or in a fast-vehicle lane, you must push your vehicle out of the way or off the road in order to not obstruct traffic.
If the traffic light turns red or yellow just as a driver is approaching an intersection or there is a police officer instructing them to stop, they must stop single file behind the stop line.
Drivers may speed through an intersection if the light has just turned yellow, even if they have not yet crossed the stop line.
Motorcycles should slow down before approaching a pedestrian crossing without a traffic control signal.
When a motorcycle approaches a pedestrian crossing where there isn't a traffic control sign, it is okay to speed through simply by honking the horn to warn the pedestrians.
Vehicles may not turn right on a red light, if the intersection does not have a right-turn arrow.
Drivers may hold the steering wheel with one hand and a cigarette with the other hand.
No matter how exhausted drivers are, they may continue to drive without any concerns about safety as long as they drive slowly.
Driving cautiously is the best way for drivers to protect their safety.
Zebra crossing is a path across a busy street designated for pedestrians to cross safely.

When two red lights start flashing alternately at a railroad grade crossing, it is considered a red light; therefore, vehicles and pedestrians should stop moving forward and wait for the train to pass.
A slow vehicle driver or pedestrian who is cited and fails to attend traffic safety classes will be fined NTD 600~1,200.
The difference of radius between inner wheels of large vehicles depends on the “wheelbase” and the “turning angle” of each vehicle.
Alcohol increases the field of vision of motorcyclists.
“Yield to pedestrians” indicates that all other traffic should respect pedestrians’ rights to cross the road first.
Because the bodies of large vehicles are taller, the drivers’ field of vision has smaller blind spots, and nearby motorcycles can be seen clearly.
Road markings do not increase the chance of motorcycles sliding during rainy days.
When motorcycles encounter emergency vehicles that are on duty, according to the regulations, motorcycles do not need to yield.
When riding motorcycles, motorcyclists only need to pay attention to the fuel level; there is no need to do extra maintenance at a set time or after a set mileage.
The best way to avoid collisions is to maintain a safe following distance from the car ahead.
Reaction distance refers to the distance which allows time needed by the driver to respond during sudden occurrences.
When followoing another vehicle, the smallest following distance should be longer than the stopping distance.
Green light gives you the permission to pass but does not necessarily ensure safety. Therefore, reduce the speed when approaching an intersection.

When the light is turning yellow at an intersection, it is the best to brake lightly and reduce the speed to give advanced notice to the motorist behind and allow time for the motorist to react to avoid collisions.

When passing a vehicle on the road without two double lanes with a broken yellow line, the time and distance for passing should be noted, the longer you are staying on the opposite lane, the more possibility for having an accident.

On a straight section of the road marked with double yellow solid lines, it is acceptable to enter the lane on the opposite direction to pass the vehicles ahead when there is no traffic traveling from the opposite direction.

Turn on the left turn signal when passing a vehicle and keep a minimum of 50cm distance to the left of the vehicle ahead. After reaching a safe distance, turn on the right turning signal and return to the original lane.
Leave ample time and space for changing directions or passing other vehicles.
Driving is a skill that requires the coordination between the hands and the brain. It is stressful and tiring. Driver safety can only be ensured by keeping a routine schedule.
Before riding a motorcycle, keep the mind clear and the body healthy. Stay focused while riding the motorcycle to respond to any possible situations.
Taking a large dosage of cold medicine or sedative does not affect a motorist's condition while operating a vehicle.
Field of vision is the limit of visibility that the motorist can perceive of the surrounding when staring straight ahead.
Construction signs, white detour signs and construction vehicles indicate road constuction ahead. The motorist should slow down and pass through with caution.
Zigzaging is not allowed while going uphill. Turning off the engine or shifting to neutral gear while going downhill is prohibited.
When driving through a tunnel with good lighting and visibility, the motorist does not need to turn on the headlights to save energy.

When accidents occur in the tunnel, though without casualties and with the vehicles being in working condition, the vehicles shall not be moved and the scene shall remain intact in order to clarify the liability.
If a motorist fails to drive safely and responsibly, it is unfortunate for the motorist as well as the public.

Although a car breakdown on the fast lane during heavy traffic would cause traffic jam and affect traffic safety, it is acceptable to fix the car first on the spot without moving the car in order to save time.
It is not necessary to check the vehicle condition before driving, but pay attention to the instruments on the dashboard to ensure safety while driving.

The best way for "safe driving" is to start off the car slowly, turn slowly and keep a safe distance. Do not rush or speed, change lanes irresponsibly, brake suddenly, cut into other lanes, force others to let you pass, or run through a red light.
Most traffic accidents occurred because of tailgating, passing and changing lanes recklessly, force turning, and speeding to save time.
Turning without using the turning signal and without paying attention to incoming traffic from behind are the main causes of accidents during turning.
Drinking will delay the motorist's reaction time but improve the motorist's vision.
People who are tired may continue to operate a motorcycle.
When an injured person is lying on the road, call 110 or 119 to notify the police or the paramedics immediately to deal with the situation.
The government provides rewards to individuals who report accidents, assist with injured people and people who are good drivers.

Turn off the engine first when pushing the motorcycle forward or backward to adjust the parking position. Hold on to both handles with both hands, watch out for the surrounding traffic, and do not make the adjustments while sitting on the seat and pushing with the feet.

When starting the motorcycle and before accelerating, turn on the turn signal and use the side mirrors to check the surrounding traffic and make sure no other vehicles or pedestrians are nearby. Turn around to check for safety and then steadily accelerate into the designated lane.

A motorcycle should slow down when it approaches an intersection and watches both sides for traffic. When there are lights, signs or markings at the intersection, they shall be the basis of judgement for stopping or proceeding.

A motorcycle should stop in the area at the intersection marked as "motorcycle waiting zone." The motorcycle should not cross the line or stop on the cross section lane, but it can stop at the area marked as "left turn waiting zone."

At an intersection, a motorcycle should stop and wait before the stopline. When the traffic light turns green, the driver should check the surrounding traffic to prevent collision and accident with other traffic violators.

When a motorcycle reaches an intersection and the red light is switching to the green light, the impulse to accelerate is dangerous for the rider. Therefore, when the light is turning green, do not rush. Take it slow, turn to look behind and then start steadily.

When a motorcycle approaches a bus stop with passengers boarding or alighting the bus, the rider cannot pass the bus from the right regardless of how wide the road is to avoid hitting any passenger who are getting on and off.
The motorcycle should not be in a race with other vehicles on the road. Don't follow any truck and don't ride between two vehicles.
When being followed by a large vehicle behind, the motorcycle rider should be alert, increase the safe distance or let it pass first.
Due to low balance, while traveling through bumpy roads, gravel roads, muddy roads or dirt roads, the motorcycle rider should slow down and be prepared to brake.
When encountering accidents, constructions, or traffic jam, the motorcycle rider should speed up and pass through quickly.

When a motorcycle approaches a bus stop with passengers boarding or alighting the bus, the rider shall not turn sharply to pass from the right of the bus. Nor shall the rider pass the bus from the left by turning sharply to the fast lane on the left to avoid collisions with the fast-moving traffic from behind.
A motorcycle should slow down while turning to prevent from slipping and falling due to centrifugal force or gravel on the road.
Riding side by side with another vehicle is not allowed on the streets in the city, but depending on traffic conditions, it could be allowed in the countryside or on the mountain roads.
A motorcycle should turn slowly at the intersection and avoid turning with another vehicle due to the difference in the turning radius to prevent from colliding during the turn.
The motorcycle rider should be fully aware of the safety precautions. Start early instead of rushing. Being safe is more important than being on time.

A motorcycle is both a convenient and dangerous form of transportation. The best way to ensure safety is to follow traffic regulations, develop road etiquette and be familiar with defensive driving techniques. Value life, respect life and respect the right of way.
Maintaining a safe distance between the motorcycle and the vehicle ahead is the most effective way to prevent rear-end collision.
Running through the red light is one of the most common causes of traffic accidents at the intersections. It is also the most severe traffic violation.
A motorcycle should be parked at the designated parking space without obstructing other vehicles or pedestrians. Failing to do so may result in collisions.

When going through a crosswalk, the motorcycle rider should follow the traffic lights, markings, and signs to reduce the speed and yield to the pedestrians. However, it is not necessary to yield to a pedestrian running through the crosswalk during red light.

The motorcycle rider should focus on driving even when carrying a passenger. The passenger should hold on to the rider firmly. Both shall avoid chatting and not focusing on the traffic. The rider could be distracted and fail to operate the motorcycle defensively.
The motorcycle rider and the passenger should both wear a helmet and wear brightly colored clothing. Anyone who wears a jacket should zip up properly to keep the coat from being caught by other cars.

Before operating a motorcycle, the motorcycle rider should first determine the route and destination, and establish a suitable path and direction. Stay focused while operating the motorcycle. Do not make sudden stops or slow down suddenly to look for directions during the ride, which may result in rear-end collision.

A motorcycle operator should develop the habit of defensive driving. Pay attention to the traffic condition at all times and check the side mirrors every 5 seconds for the traffic condition behind to ensure safety. Avoid focusing on one target for over 2 seconds and neglecting the surrounding traffic.
A motorcycle should be operated within the designated lane as stipulated in the regulations. Avoid operating the motorcycle on the markings on a rainy day to prevent falling due to slippery surface.

Accidents on highways are handled by the National Highway Police Bureau, while accidents on expressways are handled by police offices in the county or city government where accidents occur, or other police offices designated by the National Police Agency, Ministry of Interior.

If anyone acquires their driver's license by unethical or illegal means, their driver's license will be cancelled and they will be prohibited from possessing a driver's license in the R.O.C. for 5 years.
If a driver knowingly allows another person without a driver's license to drive their vehicle, their driver's license will be suspended for 3 months.
If a driver runs a red light, their driver's license will be cancelled.
If motorcyclists fail to stay in the designated motorcycle lane, they will be fined and receive traffic violation points on their driving record.

If a drunk driver causes an accident resulting in serious injury or death, they will be fined, their driver's license cancelled, and they may not possess a driver's license in the R.O.C. again. (except for those who meet certain criteria and whose suspension has expired in accordance with the requirements stipulated by the government).

If a motorcyclist is caught using a hand-held cell phone, computer, or other similar device to call, talk, digitally communicate, or do other actions that might hinder driving safety, the motorcyclist will be fined NTD 1,000.
Drivers who do not follow directional signs will be fined and receive 1 traffic violation point on their driving record.
Driving side-by-side in one lane is extremely dangerous. Therefore, violators will be fined and receive 1 traffic violation point on their driving record.
Motorcyclists who drive on the sidewalk will be fined and receive 1 traffic violation point on their driving record.
Motorists who run through the red light will only pay a fine and not receive the 3 demerit points.
If you make a U-turn at a place where left turns are prohibited, you will be fined and receive 1 traffic violation point on your driving record.
When coming to a roundabout, it is ok to enter and make an U-turn immediately.

If you go ahead and pass another vehicle without that vehicle first moving over to allow you to pass and signaling that it is okay to do so, you will be fined and receive 1 traffic violation point on your driving record.
Riders who accumulate 6 or more demerit points for traffic violations within a year will have their license suspended for 1 month.
According to the Road Traffic Management and Penalty Act, a motorcycle rider who drives under the influence of alcohol for the second time in 10 years will be fined up to NT$90,000.
A motorcycle rider using a cell phone or other consumer electronics products while riding shall be fined for NT $3,000.

If a motorcycle owner removes the exhaust muffler on purpose, or the exhaust muffler is broken and no repair is done, it is a violation of traffic regulations. The former shall result in a tougher punishment.
If you drive drunk and cause either serious injury or death, your driver's license will be cancelled and you will be prohibited from possessing a driver's license for 3 years.

If a driver is caught driving drunk because their blood alcohol level exceeds the maximum allowed by law when driving, they will receive 2 traffic violation points on their driving record, but no other penalty.
If a minor less than 14 years old violates the Statute Governing the Punishment for Violation of Road Traffic Rules, their legal representative or guardian will be penalized instead.
Motorcycles with displacement of 50cc to 250cc are considered ordinary heavy motorcycles.
Motorcycles with displacement of 50cc or less are considered light motorcycles.
It is unlawful to counterfeit, alter, or obtain a motorcycle license plate number.
If you intend to scrap your motorcycle, you don't have to notify the Motor Vehicle Registration Department, and you may keep the license plate.
When canceling or revoking a motorcycle license plate, it should be done at a motor vehicle department and the license plate shall be submitted.
If you intend to suspend the use of your motorcycle, resume using an old motorcycle, or amend a vehicle registration, you have to register at the Motor Vehicle Registration Department.
Motorcycle owners who register vehicles at the Motor Vehicle Registration Department are required to fill out an application and submit their ID card, military ID card, or alien resident certificate.
The mentally challenged, blind, or those with epilepsy are not eligible to possess a motorcycle driver's license.
The goods loaded on a motorcycle may not extend beyond the back seat.
The goods loaded on a motorcycle may not extend more than 0.5 meters beyond the rear axle.
If a motorcycle driver's license is either suspended or cancelled, drivers may not apply for another driver's license before the suspension or cancellation expires.
If a driver illegally hits a pedestrian in the crosswalk and causes either injury or death, the driver will be subject to a 50% increase in the normal criminal liability.

The Statute Governing the Punishment for Violation of Road Traffic Rules was enacted in an effort to upgrade traffic administration and maintain an orderly flow of traffic thereby ensuring traffic safety.
If a driver dies, the party responsible for the affairs of the deceased driver is required to turn in the driver's license at the Motor Vehicle Registration Department.
Drivers may drive in oncoming lanes on roads with a double yellow line separating the traffic.
If a driver hits a person on the sidewalk and causes either injury or death, the driver will be subject to a 50% increase in the normal criminal liability.
The passengers on a motorcycle can sit sideways.
If a driver recklessly cuts off other drivers by forcing their way into a line of moving vehicles, they will be fined and receive traffic violation points on their driving record.

When a motorcycle is on the road that is not separated into fast lanes and curb lanes, remains on the two lanes on the right. However, on a one-way street, remains on the farthest left and right lanes.
When a motorcycle is on a road divided into fast lanes and curb lanes, stay on the fast lane and curb lane that are the closest to the side of the road.
Prior to taking off on their motorcycle, the driver does not have to check to see if there are any other vehicles or pedestrians nearby.
When taking off on their motorcycle, drivers have to yield to traffic and pedestrians on the road.
Motorcyclists may remove their muffler to increase their engine power (Hp).
No stopping is allowed on pedestrian crosswalks.
Although light motorcycles have room for a passenger to sit on the back of the seat, drivers are not allowed to carry passengers.

On a two-way road with lane lines separating the fast and slow lanes, motorcyclists may use either the outer fast lane or the slow lane. On multi-lane oneway roads, motorcyclists may use either the slow lane or the fast lane adjacent to the slow lane if there is more than one fast lane.

On a road with 3 lanes going in the same direction, motorcyclists are required to use a two-step turning process when turning left. On oneway roads, motorcyclists traveling in the right lane or the slow lane are required to use a two-step process when turning left. Motorcyclists in either the left lane or left slow lane are required to use a two-step process when turning right.
Light motorcycles are permitted to drive on the sidewalk provided they maintain a speed of less than 20km per hour.
Prior to riding their motorcycle, drivers should check to make sure they have their driver's license and vehicle registration with them.

Drivers must abide by the instructions shown on the signs and pavement markings. If they are on a road with no signs or pavement markings, or a road without a line separating the fast and slow lanes, they should use the outside lane.
When a vehicle is coming to a curve, slope, narrow bridge, intersection, level crossing, or road construction, passing another vehicle is prohibited.
Motorcyclists may not drive on the sidewalk.
Drivers are required to slow down on roads with no lane lines separating oncoming traffic, poor condition roads, and when oncoming traffic is approaching.
Passing is not permitted in congested areas and on roads that are under construction.
When coming to an intersection without any traffic sign, the vehicle on the main road has the right-of -way.

When a motorcycle comes to an intersection that is not divided into side roads and main roads, and if both roads contain the same number of lanes that are both straight or curved, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way.
When a motorcycle comes to an intersection without traffic signals that is not separated into side roads and main roads, the vehicle going straight should have the right-of-way.
Motorcyclists entering a circular intersection are required to yield to vehicles already traveling around the intersection.
Motorcycle drivers are required to turn on their headlight when they are driving in foggy, rainy, snowy, or dimly-lit areas.

Motorcyclists may not park in front of the entrance to an airport, train or bus station, wharf, school, recreation area, exhibition hall, sports center, market or any other public facility, including fire hydrants.
On-duty Fire engines, security vehicles, ambulances, emergency rescue vehicles, garbage trucks, and mail delivery vehicles are not subject to restrictions on temporary parking and parking locations.
When a motorcycle rider is ill or drinking alcohol beverages, traffic safety is compromised and the rider shall not ride a motorcycle.

Trains may approach from both directions. No matter which direction a train is approaching from, for safety reasons you still have to look both directions to confirm no train is coming before you drive across the railroad tracks.
No matter if it is during daytime hours, drivers are required to turn on their headlights when driving in the heavy fog.
On a road with more than 3 lanes, an ordinary heavy duty motorcycle is allowed on the lane that is the closest to the center.
As oncoming vehicles pass by each other, they should maintain a distance of at least 0.5 meters apart.
A two-wheeled 250cc or larger motorcycle is considered an ordinary heavy motorcycle.
Motorcyclists may park their motorcycle on either a pedestrian crosswalk or an intersection.
You may pass another vehicle on the right.
Drivers are required to slow down when they pass by public facilities, such as a hospital or a school.
Drivers may not honk their horn when approaching a pedestrian crossing.
Drivers are required to maintain a safe driving distance behind other vehicles.
To keep other motorists from being blinded by the glare, low beam light should be used when there is incoming traffic from the opposite direction.
Since motorcycles are small and easy to operate, it is quite safe to drive a motorcycle even if you feel tired or sick.
Drivers must abide by all special traffic signals at intersections.
Heavy motorcycles may carry one passenger on the back of the motorcycle only.
The purpose of turn signals is to indicate a change in vehicle direction in advance.
Only the motorcycle rider needs to wear a helmet. The passengers are not required to wear a helmet.
The motorcycle speed shall be based on the speed limit stated on the road signs or markings. In an area without signs or markings, the speed limit shall be 50km per hour.
If your motorcycle license plate is lost, stolen, or damaged, you are required to apply for a replacement.
Those who drive either a passenger car or motorcycle without a driver's license will be fined and be barred from driving immediately.
If left turns are prohibited, drivers can still make a U-turn.
Intersections with a flashing red light require vehicles and pedestrians to stop and look both ways carefully before proceeding forward.
It is legal to lend or borrow a motorcycle license plate for installation on a motorcycle for which that plate is not registered.
The items carried on a motorcycle may extend up to one meter beyond the front of the motorcycle.
The items carried on a motorcycle may not extend more than 1 meter beyond the rear-wheel axle.
If your motorcycle's license plate is missing or stolen, you should submit a police certified document to the Motor Vehicle Registration Department and apply for a replacement plate.
If he/she drives in the slow lane where there is a line separating fast and slow lanes, the speed shall not exceed 40 km/h.
Since traffic violation points do not go on your driver's license, it's okay to just disregard them and go ahead and break the traffic rules.
Upon seeing repair technicians closing down a road or bridge ahead, drivers should ignore this and speed up in order to pass through, so that their trip is not delayed.
When driving near parks, hospitals, and schools, motorcyclists must increase situational awareness, decrease speed, and appropriately yield to pedestrians.
It is not necessary for motorcycles to yield to fire engines, ambulances, police patrol vehicles and rescue vehicles on duty.
If an intersection has both traffic lights and a police officer instructing traffic, drivers are required to comply with the instructions given by the police officer first.
If a driver's license is suspended, the driver may apply for another license.
Goods loaded on a motorcycle may not extend more than 2 meters beyond the tail end of the motorcycle.
It is ok to carry a passenger and other cargos on a motorcycle at the same time.
Motorcycle drivers are required to drive under 50km per hour when they are on a road without lane lines separating the fast and slow lanes or separating oncoming traffic.
Motorcycle drivers are required to carry their driver's license and vehicle registration with them at all times when they are driving in case a traffic control officer or the police ask to see them.
If a planned route is closed down, drivers should follow the instructions of repair technicians, and exit that section quickly and without lingering.
Roads are absolutely safe, and so there is no need to check the traffic report before driving even in stormy weather there is no danger on the road.

During a period of torrential rain noted as by the Central Weather Bureau, rock- falls, landslides, or swollen rivers under bridges in low rivers, caused by torrential rain in the upper rivers, are all signs of road disasters. When seeing these situations, drivers should avoid them and report to the departments of Directorate General of Highways or the Police Broadcasting Service as a warning to other drivers.
An automobile refers to motor vehicles that travel on the road running instead of being powered by the rail or electric cable, including motorcycle.
Heavy duty motorcycles include ordinary heavy-duty motorcycles and large heavy-duty motorcycles

Before a license plate can be issued, the motocycle owner shall provide documents showing the manufacture, dealer or importer, and the proof of completion anti-theft identification numbers applied to the auto parts with approval from the Ministry of the Interior.
The engine specification of a motorcycle may not be modified.
The lights on a motorcycle can be spray painted or covered with tapes.
The number of exhaust pipes on a motorcycle can not be modified, but the owner can relocate the exhaust pipes from one side to the other.
The minimum age for a person taking the driving license exam for light-duty motorcycles is 16. There is no maximum age limit.
